festivals.Trndez.name: Trndez
festivals.Trndez.luck.text: Trndez! Rosehips and apricot trees give double wood for the bonfire.
festivals.Trndez.greeting: Happy Trndez, the spring bonfire festival! Bonfire wood is hidden in the farm's soil. sniff() tells you how many steps it is to the nearest piece, and dig() digs it up.
festivals.Easter.name: Easter
festivals.Easter.luck.text: Easter! All plants grow 1.5 times faster.
festivals.Easter.greeting: Christ is risen! Painted eggs are hidden all over the farm. Find them with sniff() and dig them up with dig().
festivals.Vardavar.name: Vardavar
festivals.Vardavar.luck.text: Vardavar! Water is free, and when you water, a new drop sometimes splashes into the soil.
festivals.Vardavar.greeting: Happy Vardavar, the summer water festival! Water is free today. Magic drops are hidden in the soil: find them with sniff() and dig().
festivals.Navasard.name: Navasard
festivals.Navasard.luck.text: Navasard, the ancient Armenian New Year! Watermelons don't go rotten today.
festivals.Navasard.greeting: Happy Navasard, the ancient Armenian New Year! Harvest baskets are hidden on the farm: find them with sniff() and dig().
festivals.KnowledgeDay.name: Knowledge Day
festivals.KnowledgeDay.luck.text: Knowledge Day! Eggplants give a double harvest.
festivals.KnowledgeDay.greeting: Happy Knowledge Day, the first day of school! Books are hidden on the farm: find them with sniff() and dig().
festivals.TeachersDay.name: Teacher's Day
festivals.TeachersDay.luck.text: Teacher's Day! Every fish counts double.
festivals.TeachersDay.greeting: Happy Teacher's Day! Flowers are hidden on the farm: find them with sniff() and dig(), then give them to your teacher.
festivals.NewYear.name: New Year
festivals.NewYear.luck.text: New Year! Goldfish bite 3 times more often.
festivals.NewYear.greeting: Happy New Year and Merry Christmas! Dzmer Pap, the Armenian Santa, hid the gifts on the farm: find them with sniff() and dig().
notes.list.n01.text: The treasure is hidden in the tile where x + y = 3 and x · y = 2. x is smaller than y.
notes.list.n01.hint: Write down all the pairs that add up to 3: (0, 3), (1, 2), (2, 1)… Which pair multiplies to 2?
notes.list.n02.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n02.hint: Multiplying comes before subtracting, just like in math class.
notes.list.n03.text: x = 17 % 5 and y = 20 % 6 (% means the remainder after dividing).
notes.list.n03.hint: 17 divided by 5: 5 · 3 = 15. So what's left over?
notes.list.n04.text: Secret code: every number is written 3 bigger than it really is. Treasure: (5, 4).
notes.list.n05.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n05.hint: Follow the loop step by step: 10, 7, 4… When does the condition become false?
notes.list.n06.text: x is the square root of 9, and y = x − 1.
notes.list.n07.text: The numbers are written in Greek letters: α = 0, β = 1, γ = 2, δ = 3, ε = 4. Treasure: (δ, β).
notes.list.n07.hint: Find each letter's number in the list.
notes.list.n08.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n08.hint: x starts at 1, then grows by 2. y is worked out with the new x.
notes.list.n09.text: x + y = 7, x · y = 12, and x is bigger than y.
notes.list.n09.hint: Which two numbers add up to 7 and multiply to 12? Try 1 · 6, 2 · 5…
notes.list.n10.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n10.hint: The loop runs for i = 0, 1, 2 and 3. How many times does x grow?
notes.list.n11.text: Secret code: every number is multiplied by 2. Treasure: (8, 2).
notes.list.n12.hint: Work out x first, then y: that's x doubled.
notes.list.n13.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n13.hint: 5 > 3 is true, so the code inside the if runs.
notes.list.n14.text: Secret code: the numbers are flipped: 0 → 5, 1 → 4, 2 → 3, 3 → 2, 4 → 1, 5 → 0. Treasure: (0, 1).
notes.list.n14.hint: If a real 5 is written as 0, then a written 0 is really…
notes.list.n15.text: x is the third prime number (the primes are 2, 3, …), and y = x − 2.
notes.list.n15.hint: A prime number can only be divided by 1 and by itself. 4 isn't prime (4 = 2 · 2).
notes.list.n16.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n16.hint: f(2) means n = 2. Work out n · 2 + 1.
notes.list.n17.text: In the Fibonacci sequence (1, 1, 2, 3, …), each number is the sum of the two before it. x is the 5th number in it, and y is the 3rd.
notes.list.n18.text: The numbers are written in binary: x = 100, y = 101.
notes.list.n19.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n19.hint: List positions start at 0: a[0] is 4.
notes.list.n20.hint: Which number times itself makes 36? And 25?
notes.list.n21.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n21.hint: x gets 1, 2 and 3 added to it, and y gets 2 added every time.
notes.list.n22.text: Letter code: a = 0, b = 1, c = 2, … Treasure: (g, c).
notes.list.n22.hint: Count the letters: a, b, c, d, e, f, g…
notes.list.n23.text: x is half of the greatest common divisor of 24 and 36, and y = x − 6.
notes.list.n23.hint: What's the biggest number that divides both 24 and 36 with no remainder?
notes.list.n24.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n25.hint: Multiply first, then subtract or add.
notes.list.n26.text: Secret code: 4 was taken away from every number. Treasure: (3, 3).
notes.list.n27.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n28.text: x is the biggest prime number below 10, and y = 8 / 2.
notes.list.n28.hint: A prime number can only be divided by 1 and by itself. 9 isn't prime (9 = 3 · 3).
notes.list.n29.text: Run this program in your head (or with say()). At the end, x and y point to the treasure's tile.
notes.list.n29.hint: Follow n: 12, 6, 3, 1.5… Each step, x grows by 1.
notes.list.n30.text: The numbers are written in Roman numerals: x = IX, y = III.
notes.list.n30.hint: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10. When a smaller numeral comes before a bigger one, you subtract it.
notes.list.n31.text: The treasure is hidden under the pomegranate with the most seeds. When you dig, that pomegranate must still be growing on the farm.
notes.list.n31.hint: scan() on a pomegranate tells you how many seeds it has. Scan them all and remember where the biggest number is.
notes.list.n32.text: The treasure is one step to the right of the sweetest grapevine.
notes.list.n32.hint: scan() on a grapevine tells you how sweet it is. Find the sweetest one and go one step right.
notes.list.n33.text: The treasure is in the bottom-left corner of the biggest giant square watermelon.
notes.list.n33.hint: A giant square watermelon covers several tiles. Its bottom-left tile has the smallest x and the smallest y.
notes.list.n34.text: The treasure is in the bottom row (y = 0), and x is the number of ponds on your farm.
notes.list.n34.hint: Visit every tile and use soilType() to count the Soils.Pond tiles.
notes.list.n35.text: The treasure is in the bottom row (y = 0), and x is the last digit of how much gold you have in storage (gold % 10).
notes.list.n35.hint: count(Goods.Gold) tells you how much gold you have, and % 10 gives you the last digit.
